rationale: C14 provides a concrete, nearly verbatim drafting template: the same two-recital sequence first identifies an official who will become subject to compulsory retirement under the same statute unless exempted by Executive order, then invokes the public interest to justify exemption. Only the official, office, and retirement month are materially changed. C16 and C07 use the same machinery and language but are slightly weaker alternatives.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS John J. Deviny, the Public Printer, will, during the month of June, 1952, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS Frances Perkins, a member of the United States Civil Service Commission, will, during the month of April 1952 become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.explanation: This is the same distinctive factual-and-legal recital with the person, office, and month substituted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below: NOW THEREFORE
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below: NOW THEREFORE
shared_material.explanation: The justification recital and transition into the operative provisions are essentially verbatim and occur in the same sequence.
